rows.title: A phone typed with an extension or a second number gets a clickable tel: link that dials a wrong, merged number
rows.summary: Now: contactHref's phone link (telHref in src/utils/contacts.js) dials the first number only, cut at '/', ',', ';', '|' or 'or' once seven digits are in (so '030/1234567' stays one number), with an extension (ext., extension, x, #) as RFC 3966 ';ext='. '+1 (555) 123-4567 ext. 890' links to tel:+15551234567;ext=890 and '+91 98765 43210 / +91 91234 56789' to tel:+919876543210, in the PDF, Word and Markdown. The printed text is unchanged. docs/knowledge/03-data-model.md notes it.

rows.title: A website/LinkedIn/GitHub 'Link URL' box holding only 'https://' (or 'www.') removes the contact's link, although the typed value is a good link
rows.summary: Now: a new linkOverride helper (src/utils/contacts.js) gives the Link URL only when safeHref accepts it. Otherwise ('https://', 'www.', a javascript: address) the box counts as empty, and contactHref links the typed value. The ATS text, cover-letter text and JSON Resume export use the same helper, so every format agrees. docs/knowledge/03-data-model.md notes it.

issues: R5-HUNT12-REVIEW-TEL-EXT-BRACKET-COMMA (defect in a52ea499): the extension was read only right after the number, so '+1 555 123 4567 (ext 12)' still linked to tel:+1555123456712 (the merged number the fix set out to end) and '(555) 123-4567, ext. 890' was cut at the comma and lost its extension. Fixed in caa004e0: an extension in brackets, or after the separator, stays with its number as ;ext=.

R5-HUNT12-REVIEW-TEL-TRUNK-ZERO (next to a52ea499, there before it): '+44 (0) 20 7946 0958' linked to tel:+4402079460958, which does not dial. Fixed in 9a3e52af: after a '+', a bracketed trunk (0) is left out of the link. A national '(0) 20 ...' keeps its 0.

R5-HUNT12-REVIEW-IMPORT-PHONE-OWN-TEL-LINK (caused by a52ea499 and 9a3e52af): the import kept a linked phone's text only when the link held exactly its digits. Once the link dials only the first number and drops the trunk 0, the app's own Markdown/PDF/Word export of '+91 98765 43210 / +91 91234 56789' or '+44 (0) 20 7946 0958' imported as the link's bare digits. Fixed in 05f823c3: linkParts keeps the text when the link is the one contactHref writes for it.

R5-HUNT12-REVIEW-IMPORT-PHONE-EXTENSION (there before the branch, and it made the new ;ext= links pointless on a round trip): the import's PHONE test rejected letters, so a phone with an extension ('... ext. 890', 'x12', '(ext 12)') came back as no phone at all, from pasted text or from the app's own exports. Fixed in 162012c5: PHONE_EXT reads the number before the extension and keeps the value as typed.

f8e4142f (linkOverride) reviewed clean. A javascript:/bare-scheme Link URL now falls back to the typed value's link in contactHref, the ATS text, the letter text and JSON Resume alike. The existing javascript: tests (markdown-export-contacts, r5-hunt4 ATS, r5-hunt6 JSON Resume, 98-exp/r5hunt6 letter text) still hold; the editor never reads the override on its own.
